column2: The inside wall of a 1980s New York record store: tall wooden shelves packed floor to ceiling with vinyl LP sleeves facing out in hot pink, cyan, yellow and black, eye flower designs on many sleeves, hand lettered genre cards, a strip of pink neon along the top, posters taped between shelves.

The ground floor and first storey of a row of red brick Greenwich Village walk-up tenements in winter 1963: shop windows glowing warm, stone stoops with snow, black iron fire escapes, snow on every ledge, a barber pole, a coffee house door.

The ground and first storeys of East Village tenements in 1975: a basement clothing shop with racks, stone stoops, painted brick, layers of torn gig posters with eye flowers, a fire escape, a hand painted sign.

A Lower East Side street wall in 1989: a row of storefronts with striped awnings, roll down steel shutters covered in colourful graffiti and eye flower tags, hand painted shop signs, racks of t shirts, a bodega fruit stand, a pay phone.

The wall of a 1977 Bowery punk club: every inch covered in layers of band stickers, torn flyers, scrawled marker and spray paint, photocopied gig posters with eye flowers, a dented pay phone, dim red light.

The painted cinder block wall of a Bronx community room in 1973: a huge hand painted graffiti mural of bubble letters and eye flowers in bright colours, a bulletin board, a clock, folding chairs stacked against the wall, a party flyer.

A row of four storey Harlem brownstones in 1958 seen straight on: brownstone facades with tall windows, ornate cornices, iron railings and stoops, potted plants on the sills, a corner shop with an awning.

The red wall of a basement jazz club: deep red paint, rows of framed black and white photographs of musicians playing horns, bass and piano, every musician with an eye flower head, small brass picture lamps over each frame.

The side wall of a grand historic Harlem theatre: tiers of gilded opera boxes with red velvet curtains, gold plaster ornament, red damask wallpaper, little lamps on each box, cheering audience in the boxes with eye flower heads.

A wall of a bohemian New York hotel lobby crowded floor to ceiling with paintings in mismatched gilt frames, a salon hang of abstract canvases, surreal eye flower portraits, small sculptures on brackets, a brass plaque, warm lamp light.
